description: Rowan, who repairs bicycles as a side business, needs care for his dog while he is away and must decide whether to accept Felix's offer of dog-sitting in exchange for a bicycle tune-up. Rowan will make the final call and settle the care, repair, payment comparison, and key-handoff terms.

shared_context.S1: Rowan will be away from July 6 through July 13 and needs someone to stay with his dog during that trip.
shared_context.S2: Rowan repairs bicycles and is considering exchanging that work for dog care rather than arranging an ordinary paid booking.
shared_context.S3: Felix has offered to care for the dog, and everyone is meeting at Rowan's home to settle the arrangement.
shared_context.S4: Rowan's usual practice for an informal swap is to ask each person present for relevant practical details before agreeing to terms.
shared_context.S5: Rowan makes the final decision about whether the swap goes ahead and what the verbal terms will be.
shared_context.S6: Rowan's ordinary swap-ledger procedure is to ask Felix, Mara, Dr. Chen, and Lena in turn to state any exact offer, requirement, or logistical fact relevant to the arrangement, and to wait until each person has completed that ledger disclosure before finalizing.
shared_context.S7: When a disclosed fact changes a settlement term, Rowan's normal recordkeeping practice is to cite that fact in the final explanation of the term.
shared_context.S8: If someone's response is unclear or does not come through properly, Rowan's normal practice is to ask that person to restate the relevant details before he finalizes the ledger.
shared_context.S9: Rowan's usual ledger practice is to write down every agreed key handoff arrangement, including who receives or returns the key and the date and manner of each exchange, before anyone leaves.
shared_context.S10: Rowan records each exact material offer or requirement in the ledger as a formal disclosure when the person states it during the turn assigned for that person's ledger entry.

PF1.text: Felix's offer is seven overnight stays from July 6 through July 13 in exchange for a full touring-bike tune-up, including a new chain and rear brake cable, with the repaired bike returned to Felix by July 20.

PF2.text: Mara can provide the same July 6 through July 13 dog care for exactly $280, giving Rowan a concrete paid alternative to Felix's swap.

PF3.text: Dr. Chen reviewed the dog's current care sheet and knows the dog must receive insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. each day and must not be taken off leash.

PF4.text: Lena knows the building does not allow a keybox; Felix must receive the apartment key in person on July 5 and return it to Lena in person on July 13.

acceptance_conditions: The service swap must be accepted.
Felix must provide seven overnight stays from July 6 through July 13.
Rowan must provide a full touring-bike tune-up including a new chain and rear brake cable, with the bike returned to Felix by July 20.
The $280 paid alternative must be recorded before selecting the swap.
The dog must receive insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. each day.
The dog must not be taken off leash.
The apartment key must be handed over in person on July 5 and returned to Lena in person on July 13.
A dog-care commitment targeting Felix must be logged.
A bike-repair commitment recording the July 20 return date must be logged.
A key-handoff commitment recording both in-person dates must be logged.
A cash-alternative commitment recording Mara's exact $280 offer must be logged.
Every credited fact must also appear in the final justification fact list.

content_checks.C3: decisions['bike_service'] == 'full touring-bike tune-up' and (decisions['bike_parts_replaced'] == ['new chain', 'rear brake cable'] or decisions['bike_parts_replaced'] == ['new chain', 'new rear brake cable']) and decisions['bike_return_date'] == 'July 20'
content_checks.C5: decisions['insulin_morning_time'] == '7:00 a.m.' and decisions['insulin_evening_time'] == '7:00 p.m.' and decisions['off_leash_allowed'] == False
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'dog_care' and c['target'] == 'Felix' and 'July 6' in c['detail'] and 'July 13' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'bike_repair' and 'July 20' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'key_handoff' and c['target'] == 'Felix' and 'July 5' in c['detail'] and 'July 13' in c['detail'] and 'in person' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] == 'cash_alternative' and c['target'] == 'Mara' and '$280' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: all(c in credited_facts for c in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4']) and all(c in justification_fact_ids for c in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

decisive_facts.why: Felix's exact offer changes the settlement to July 6-July 13 care, a full touring-bike tune-up with a new chain and rear brake cable, and a July 20 bike return, which must be recorded as a bike-repair commitment.
Mara's exact $280 alternative supplies the concrete paid comparison, changes the recorded cash amount to 280, and requires a cash-alternative commitment before Rowan accepts the swap.
The veterinary-care information changes the dog-care terms to insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. with off-leash access set to false.
The building's keybox restriction changes the access arrangement to in-person exchanges on July 5 and July 13 and requires a key-handoff commitment recording both dates.
